{"choices":[{"finish_reason":"tool_calls","index":0,"message":{"content":"My changes are complete and match the canonical upstream fix (commit `341a19e`) for ripgrep issue #2574. Let me summarize what I did:

## Summary

### Problem
When using the `--word-regexp` (`-w`) flag, ripgrep was producing incomplete/incorrect matches. For the pattern `([\w]+[.])*domain[.](\w)+` against `some.domain.com/x`, it matched `ome.domain.com` (starting from the second character) instead of `some.domain.com`.

### Root Cause
The `-w` flag is implemented by wrapping the user's pattern as `(?m:^|\W)(<original>)(?m:$|\W)` (rather than `\b(<original>)\b`, because `\b` has unintuitive behavior when the pattern matches non-word characters at boundaries). The actual match (the user's pattern) is at capture group 1.

To avoid the slower capture-group-extracting regex engine, `WordMatcher::fast_find` in `crates/regex/src/word.rs` has a "fast path" that:
1. Finds the overall match.
2. Strips the first and last characters (assuming they're `\W` boundary characters).
3. Verifies the original regex matches the stripped result.

The bug: the fast path only bailed to the slow engine when the match was at the very start (`cand.start() == 0`) or end (`cand.end() == haystack.len()`) of the haystack. But the `^`/`$` line anchors (`StartLF`/`EndLF`) also match at line boundaries *within* the haystack (after/before `\n`). When a match started at an internal line boundary via `^` (consuming no character), the fast path still stripped the first character â which was actually part of the user's match â yielding an incorrect, shifted match offset.

### Fix
In `fast_find`, after finding the candidate match, decode the characters at the start and end of the match. If either character is a **word character**, then `\W` could not have matched it, meaning the `^`/`$` anchor matched instead. In that case, defer to the slower (correct) capture-extracting engine.

This is the canonical upstream fix (ripgrep commit `341a19e`, "regex: fix fast path for -w/--word-regexp flag (#2576)", fixing issue #2574).

### Files Changed
1. **`crates/regex/src/word.rs`** â The core fix in `fast_find`: check whether the boundary characters are word characters and bail to the slow engine if so.
2. **`tests/regression.rs`** â Added the `r2574` regression test (added via shell append to preserve the file's tab characters, which the editor tool would otherwise normalize).
3. **`CHANGELOG.md`** â Added a bug-fix entry referencing issue #2574.

### Verification
- The PR's reproduction case now correctly matches `some.domain.com` on all three lines, consistent with the `\b`-wrapped behavior.
- All 285 integration tests pass (including the new `r2574`), plus all workspace unit tests, both with and without the `pcre2` feature.
- Existing word-matching tests (`misc::word`, `r506_word_not_parenthesized`, `r1891`) and the `grep-regex` unit tests (`various_find`, `various_captures`, `regression_dash`, `capture_indexing`) all still pass.","role":"assistant","tool_calls":[{"function":{"arguments":"{}","name":"submit"},"id":"call_-7373169772927646747","index":0,"type":"function"}]}}],"created":1786078810,"id":"20260807125958287a82c7f5c145b6","model":"glm-5.2","object":"chat.completion","request_id":"20260807125958287a82c7f5c145b6","usage":{"completion_tokens":766,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens":99166,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":98176},"total_tokens":99932}}
